link:https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pon.reader_title: Collaboration and funding are both associated with less novel research, not more
link:https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pon.reader_what: Across European regions, scientific collaboration and research funding both correlate negatively with novelty.
link:https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pon.reader_why: Challenges the assumption that collaborative funded research automatically produces more original work.
link:https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pon.reader_more: This study uses Web of Science publication data from European regions between 2008 and 2017 to test how collaboration and funding relate to the novelty of research, measuring collaboration at five levels from country through three regional tiers to institutions, and measuring novelty through keyword combinations. The headline results run against common assumptions: there is a negative and significant relationship between scientific collaboration and novelty, and funded papers show lower novelty than unfunded ones. Funding does, however, have a significant moderating effect on the relationship between collaboration and novelty. The authors position the contribution as linking multiple levels of collaboration and funding source to novelty within bibliometric research.

deep_analysis.research_question: How scientific collaboration and research funding relate to the novelty of research output in European regions.
deep_analysis.main_finding: Scientific collaboration is negatively and significantly related to novelty, funded papers show lower novelty than unfunded ones, and funding significantly moderates the collaboration-novelty relationship.
deep_analysis.method_or_basis: Analysis of Web of Science publications from European regions, 2008 to 2017, with collaboration measured at five levels and novelty measured from keyword combinations.
deep_analysis.qualification: Novelty operationalised through keyword combinations is a proxy that may penalise incremental but valuable work; these are associations, and funded research may be selected for different goals than novelty.
deep_analysis.radar_relevance: Questions whether the collaborative, funded model dominant in European research policy delivers original knowledge.

link:https://doi.org/10.1016/j.trip.2021.reader_title: Commission pilot applied horizon scanning to transport research priorities
link:https://doi.org/10.1016/j.trip.2021.reader_what: Pilot within a Commission transport monitoring system identified emerging technologies and future research needs.
link:https://doi.org/10.1016/j.trip.2021.reader_why: Highlighted energy and transport interaction as an area requiring research investment.
link:https://doi.org/10.1016/j.trip.2021.reader_more: This paper reports a horizon scanning pilot run inside the Commission's Transport Research and Innovation Monitoring and Information System, an open-access tool supporting the Strategic Transport Research and Innovation Agenda across all transport modes. The exercise was structured and collaborative, aimed at identifying emerging technologies and trends and assessing current and future research needs, with results feeding into wider Commission policy. It surfaced the significance of interaction between the energy and transport sectors and four challenges identified in an expert workshop: radical alternatives to cars in cities, electrification and rising power demand, fleet modernisation through retrofitting, and automation that maintains the current system with fewer externalities.

deep_analysis.work_kind: peer-reviewed methods and application paper by the tool's developers
deep_analysis.research_question: How horizon scanning can be applied within an EU transport research monitoring system to identify emerging technologies and research needs.
deep_analysis.main_finding: The pilot identified disruptive mobility technologies and four priority challenges, and highlighted energy and transport sector interaction as requiring research investment.
deep_analysis.method_or_basis: Structured collaborative horizon scanning exercise with an expert workshop, conducted within the Commission's transport monitoring system.
deep_analysis.qualification: Written by the system's co-developers, so it is partly a description of their own tool; outputs are expert-generated priorities rather than validated predictions, and the exercise dates from 2021.
deep_analysis.radar_relevance: A worked example of foresight methodology applied directly inside EU research policy machinery.

link:https://doi.org/10.1093/etojnl/vgag.reader_title: Proposal for a shared practice community to spot emerging environmental health risks earlier
link:https://doi.org/10.1093/etojnl/vgag.reader_what: Proposes a horizon scanning community of practice to replace slow, fragmented risk identification.
link:https://doi.org/10.1093/etojnl/vgag.reader_why: Identifies shared features of effective scanning: clear objectives, flexible communication, diverse stakeholders.
link:https://doi.org/10.1093/etojnl/vgag.reader_more: This commentary synthesises a 2024 workshop convened by the United States National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences and proposes building a horizon scanning community of practice for emerging environmental health risks. It addresses three problems identified at the workshop: slow risk assessment, fragmented data systems and limited cross-agency communication. It reviews existing frameworks including the Delphi method and a United States regulatory council's contaminants of emerging concern framework, concluding that effective models share clear objectives, structured but flexible communication and inclusion of diverse stakeholders including non-traditional experts and affected communities. The recommended route is transdisciplinary collaboration, shared data standards and starting with focused, scalable efforts. The institutional setting is American, so transferability to European structures is assumed rather than demonstrated.

deep_analysis.research_question: How horizon scanning capacity for emerging environmental health risks can be organised more effectively.
deep_analysis.main_finding: Effective horizon scanning frameworks share clear objectives, structured but flexible communication and diverse stakeholder inclusion, and a community of practice built on transdisciplinary collaboration and shared data standards could shift risk identification from reactive to proactive.
deep_analysis.method_or_basis: Synthesis of a 2024 expert workshop plus review of existing horizon scanning frameworks.
deep_analysis.qualification: A proposal rather than an evaluated intervention, grounded in United States agencies and frameworks; its applicability to European institutional arrangements is not tested.
deep_analysis.radar_relevance: Method contribution: identifies design features of horizon scanning systems relevant to how this Radar itself operates.

link:https://doi.org/10.1007/s43621-026-.reader_title: Systematic review of factors underpinning dairy sector foresight in emerging economies
link:https://doi.org/10.1007/s43621-026-.reader_what: Review classifies 44 factors used in dairy foresight, dominated by economic and environmental considerations.
link:https://doi.org/10.1007/s43621-026-.reader_more: This systematic review identifies the factors underpinning foresight scenarios for sustainable dairy development in emerging countries, following the PRISMA 2020 protocol. Kenya and India supplied the most included articles. The authors extract 44 factors and classify them into five categories: social, technological, economic, environmental and policy. Economic and environmental factors dominate, appearing in 78 and 72 percent of studies respectively, while social factors appear in only about 44 percent, which the authors treat as an imbalance in how the sector's futures are constructed. The work is a methodological contribution to foresight practice in agricultural systems; its subject matter is dairy development in emerging economies rather than European research and innovation, so its relevance here is confined to method.

deep_analysis.research_question: Which factors inform foresight scenarios for sustainable dairy sector development across emerging countries.
deep_analysis.main_finding: Forty-four factors group into five categories, with economic and environmental factors dominating at 78 and 72 percent of studies while social factors appear in only 44 percent.
deep_analysis.method_or_basis: Systematic literature review using PRISMA 2020, covering identification and selection, quality assessment and analysis.
deep_analysis.qualification: Counts how often factor types appear in the literature, which measures research attention rather than the factors' actual importance; evidence concentrates on Kenya and India.
deep_analysis.radar_relevance: Method contribution only: it illustrates how foresight factor sets are constructed, with no European research and innovation content.

link:https://doi.org/10.1016/j.array.202.reader_title: AI tool surfaced food safety risks years before formal European recognition
link:https://doi.org/10.1016/j.array.202.reader_what: Retrospective tests show the tool flagged two contamination risks well before EU food safety opinions.
link:https://doi.org/10.1016/j.array.202.reader_why: Demonstrates automated weak signal detection complementing expert-based emerging risk identification.
link:https://doi.org/10.1016/j.array.202.reader_more: This paper presents the Weak Signal Miner, an AI pipeline for detecting early-stage signals of emerging food and feed safety risks in large text collections. It combines transformer-based micro-topic modelling, adaptive temporal aggregation and a scoring scheme weighting recency and magnitude to find rare topics showing disproportionate recent growth, with an optional large language model layer adding labels and novelty and severity scores to support rather than replace expert judgement. Retrospective testing is the substantive evidence: the tool surfaced signals on perfluorooctanesulfonic acid contamination between 2004 and 2007, and citrinin in red yeast rice supplements between 2010 and 2017, in both cases well before formal recognition in a European Food Safety Authority opinion.

deep_analysis.work_kind: peer-reviewed method development paper with retrospective validation
deep_analysis.research_question: Whether automated weak signal mining can identify emerging food and feed safety risks earlier than expert-based processes.
deep_analysis.main_finding: The pipeline retrospectively surfaced two known contamination risks well ahead of their formal recognition in European Food Safety Authority opinions, supporting weak signal mining as a data-driven complement to expert risk identification.
deep_analysis.method_or_basis: Transformer-based micro-topic modelling with temporal aggregation and recency-magnitude scoring, optionally interpreted by large language models, tested retrospectively on two historical cases.
deep_analysis.qualification: Retrospective validation on two known cases risks hindsight selection and says nothing about false positive rates in live operation, where the practical cost is analyst time spent on spurious signals.
deep_analysis.radar_relevance: Method contribution directly applicable to automated scanning of the kind this Radar performs.

link:https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jtrangeo..reader_title: Randomly selected citizens added equity and privacy concerns to Berlin mobility scenarios
link:https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jtrangeo..reader_what: Fifty randomly selected residents surfaced inclusivity, flexibility, data protection and equity concerns in scenario work.
link:https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jtrangeo..reader_why: Shows deliberative methods can widen what strategic foresight processes treat as relevant.
link:https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jtrangeo..reader_more: This paper examines what happens when randomly selected citizens are integrated into a formal exploratory scenario process, an approach less studied than participatory scenario work generally. It reports three-day planning cells held at the EUREF Campus in Berlin within the Mobility2Grid urban living lab, in which 50 randomly selected residents helped develop mobility scenarios for Berlin in 2045. The finding is that while methodological adaptation was required, involving citizens in evaluating future projections enriched the process with everyday perspectives and surfaced concerns that included inclusivity, flexibility, data protection and social equity. The authors discuss both the potential and the limitations of embedding deliberative methods within strategic foresight.

deep_analysis.research_question: How randomly selected citizens can be integrated into formalised exploratory scenario processes, and with what effect.
deep_analysis.main_finding: Citizen planning cells enriched scenario development with everyday perspectives and surfaced inclusivity, flexibility, data protection and social equity as key concerns, though methodological adaptation was needed.
deep_analysis.method_or_basis: Three-day planning cells with 50 randomly selected residents within a Berlin urban living lab, feeding a systematic exploratory scenario process for 2045.
deep_analysis.qualification: A single city and single living lab; the reported enrichment is the authors' qualitative assessment rather than a comparison against an equivalent expert-only process.
deep_analysis.radar_relevance: Method contribution on integrating public deliberation into foresight, relevant to how research priorities are set.

link:https://doi.org/10.1007/s44498-026-.reader_title: Method for finding policies that stay reliable when the data is too thin to model precisely
link:https://doi.org/10.1007/s44498-026-.reader_what: Proposes shifting from most probable outcomes to policies that remain robust across wide uncertainty ranges.
link:https://doi.org/10.1007/s44498-026-.reader_why: Argues conventional uncertainty analysis overstates knowledge when empirical evidence is scarce.
link:https://doi.org/10.1007/s44498-026-.reader_more: This study proposes a framework for evaluating policy in material flow analysis under deep uncertainty, motivated by the observation that conventional uncertainty methods can overstate available knowledge when data is scarce, characterising uncertainty beyond what the evidence supports. The proposed shift is away from identifying the most probable outcomes and towards identifying policies that remain reliable despite uncertainty, achieved by integrating material flow analysis with exploratory modelling that spans broad plausible ranges including extreme scenarios and assesses performance across multiple robustness metrics. The paper also offers technical solutions for handling the constraint that transfer coefficients must sum to one. An illustrative case study demonstrates the framework under simplified conditions, and the authors state further work is needed before systematic application.

deep_analysis.research_question: How to evaluate policy robustly in material flow analysis when data scarcity produces deep uncertainty.
deep_analysis.main_finding: The authors propose replacing most-probable-outcome analysis with robustness-based evaluation across broad plausible uncertainty ranges, and supply methods for handling the sum-to-one constraint on transfer coefficients.
deep_analysis.method_or_basis: Integration of material flow analysis with exploratory modelling and analysis, demonstrated through an illustrative simplified case study.
deep_analysis.qualification: The authors state explicitly that the case study is illustrative under simplified conditions and that further research is needed before systematic practical application.
deep_analysis.radar_relevance: Method contribution on reasoning about policy under deep uncertainty, applicable to foresight beyond material flows.

link:https://doi.org/10.1093/forestry/cp.reader_title: Framework for combining AI signal detection with expert judgement in horizon scanning
link:https://doi.org/10.1093/forestry/cp.reader_what: Proposes six-stage AI-assisted horizon scanning combining automated signal discovery with expert deliberation.
link:https://doi.org/10.1093/forestry/cp.reader_why: Addresses data gaps and institutional fragmentation that currently limit AI use in this sector.
link:https://doi.org/10.1093/forestry/cp.reader_more: Building on a 2022 national horizon scan that identified catastrophic forest ecosystem collapse as the most pressing emerging issue, this paper asks how AI could strengthen foresight and policy coherence in United Kingdom forestry. The authors note that although large language models existed during that 2022 exercise, their use in environmental foresight was not yet methodologically normalised, which they read as evidence of a fast-changing methodological context rather than an omission. They propose a six-stage framework combining AI-enabled signal detection with expert interpretation and deliberation: framing, signal discovery, expert engagement, synthesis, simulation and reflexive learning, operationalising responsible research and AI principles. They also advance a forestry foresight lab linking government, research and landowners through federated data commons.

deep_analysis.research_question: How artificial intelligence can strengthen horizon scanning and foresight for forest resilience policy.
deep_analysis.main_finding: The authors propose a six-stage AI-assisted horizon scanning framework pairing automated signal detection with expert deliberation, governed by responsible research and AI principles, plus an institutional foresight lab built on federated data commons.
deep_analysis.method_or_basis: Methodological proposal building on a 2022 national horizon scan, with framework design rather than empirical testing.
deep_analysis.qualification: The framework is proposed and not yet implemented or evaluated; it is developed for United Kingdom forestry with devolved administrations in view, so transfer to other sectors or jurisdictions is untested.
deep_analysis.radar_relevance: Method contribution on pairing automated scanning with human judgement, directly analogous to this Radar's own design.

link:https://doi.org/10.34190/eckm.27.1..reader_title: Multi-agent language model system turning patents into competitive intelligence reports
link:https://doi.org/10.34190/eckm.27.1..reader_what: Eight-role agent system converts patent filings into structured intelligence reports with market evidence.
link:https://doi.org/10.34190/eckm.27.1..reader_why: Separates generating and evaluating models so no system judges its own output.
link:https://doi.org/10.34190/eckm.27.1..reader_more: This paper presents an eight-role multi-agent system that turns disclosed patent filings plus a free-text intelligence request into a structured competitive intelligence report. The system treats patents as seed signals, searches the open web for corresponding market evidence such as products, vendors, deployments and partnerships, and reports honestly when no evidence is found. Six frontier models execute the generative roles in parallel, while an independent pool of different models operates verifier, telemetry and judge roles, preserving the principle that the model evaluating an output is never the one that produced it. Evaluation covers four heterogeneous patent filings, reporting per-model precision, recall, semantic alignment and calibration error alongside cost and elapsed time.

deep_analysis.work_kind: peer-reviewed conference paper presenting a system with evaluation
deep_analysis.research_question: Whether a multi-agent large language model system can automate the technology intelligence lifecycle from patents to market signals.
deep_analysis.main_finding: The authors demonstrate an eight-role architecture that produces structured intelligence reports with separated generation and evaluation roles, reported against precision, recall, semantic alignment and calibration metrics on four test filings.
deep_analysis.method_or_basis: System implementation on a multi-agent framework with six frontier models in generative roles and two independent models as verifier, telemetry and judge, evaluated on four patent filings.
deep_analysis.qualification: Evaluation on only four filings is a very small test set; using language models as judges of other language models remains a contested evaluation method despite the separation of roles.
deep_analysis.radar_relevance: Method contribution on automated technology intelligence, closely analogous to the automatic scanning stage of this Radar.
